items.title: Asian markets rally on RBA rate hike, US-India trade deal

featured_image.name: Asia-Pacific markets: Nikkei 225, Kospi, Hang Seng Index, Iran, Powell

items.description:
Asian equity markets surged on Tuesday as investors digested a pair of developments that brightened the economic outlook: the Reserve Bank of Australia's first interest rate hike in two years and a newly announced trade agreement between the United States and India.

Japan's Nikkei 225 climbed over 3% to reach record highs, while South Korea's Kospi rocketed 5%, triggering a buy sidecar after the index's futures rose more than 5% for over a minute. India's Nifty 50 jumped roughly 3%, approaching its all-time high, as traders responded enthusiastically to the tariff relief from Washington. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 added 1.3%, buoyed by the central bank's decisive move to combat inflation.[1][2][3]

items.title: Gold, silver rebound after historic crash on Fed chair pick

featured_image.name: Gold prices fall as Trump announces Kevin Warsh as Fed chair pick

items.description:
Gold and silver staged a recovery in Tuesday's Asian trading session after enduring one of the most violent selloffs in modern market history, a crash triggered by President Donald Trump's nomination of Kevin Warsh as Federal Reserve chair and amplified by cascading margin calls.

Spot gold climbed more than 3% to around $4,837 per ounce on Tuesday morning, rebounding from Monday's lows near $4,400. Silver jumped more than 5% to approximately $84 per ounce after testing lows below $72 earlier in the week. The recovery came as calmer conditions returned to markets that had been roiled by forced liquidations and extreme volatility.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: CATL claims new battery can fast-charge in 12 minutes

featured_image.name: CATL unveils EV battery with 323-mile range on 5-minute charge

items.description: A wave of recent advances in battery and materials engineering promises to address two persistent challenges facing electric vehicles: slow charging times and limited range. Research teams in China and South Korea have unveiled innovations that could make EVs more convenient and efficient without requiring larger, heavier battery packs.

items.title: Musk confirms SpaceX-xAI merger ahead of planned IPO

featured_image.name: Musk Is Said to Be in Advanced Talks to Combine SpaceX, xAI

items.description:
Elon Musk is combining his rocket and satellite company SpaceX with his artificial intelligence firm xAI in a corporate consolidation that could set the stage for one of the largest initial public offerings in history. The deal was announced via internal memo on Monday, according to Bloomberg News, bringing together Musk's space exploration infrastructure with his AI ambitions under a single corporate umbrella.[1][2][3]

The newly combined entity is expected to be valued at approximately $1.25 trillion, with a share price set around $527, according to Reuters citing Bloomberg's reporting. The merger comes as SpaceX prepares for a mid-June IPO that could raise as much as $50 billion and value the company at roughly $1.5 trillion, according to the Financial Times.[4][5][6][7][1]

items.title: Wall Street rises as oil, gold slide on US-Iran diplomatic thaw

featured_image.name: Dow surges 500 points as traders look past rout in precious metals and bitcoin: Live updates

items.description:
Wall Street rebounded Monday as diplomatic progress between the United States and Iran unwound the geopolitical risk premiums that had driven commodity prices higher in recent weeks. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose more than 500 points while crude oil tumbled more than 4% and precious metals extended a historic rout.

The rally came after President Donald Trump said over the weekend that Iran was "seriously talking" with Washington, and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian ordered the resumption of nuclear negotiations. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is expected to meet White House envoy Steve Witkoff on Friday in Istanbul for the first direct engagement between U.S. and Iranian officials since the collapse of talks and the 12-day conflict in June 2025.[1][2][3]

items.title: German researchers develop AI drones to locate radioactive waste in minutes

featured_image.name: German military drones, robots hunt radioactive waste in ...

items.description:
Researchers at the Fraunhofer Institute for Communication, Information Processing and Ergonomics FKIE in Germany have developed AI-powered drones and robots capable of locating radioactive sources within a few meters in just minutes, addressing one of the most dangerous challenges facing emergency responders.[1][2][3][4]

The technology, unveiled this week, aims to protect first responders and civilians from the invisible threat posed by chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, and explosive substances (CBRNE) that cannot be detected by humans from a safe distance.[2][5]

items.title: NASA pauses Artemis II fueling test after hydrogen leak detected

featured_image.name: NASA fuels Artemis II moon rocket in test to clear the way for Super ...

items.description:
NASA is conducting a high-stakes fueling test of its massive moon rocket Monday as the agency pushes toward the first crewed lunar mission in more than 50 years, though engineers have encountered a hydrogen leak that required troubleshooting during the critical rehearsal.

The wet dress rehearsal, which began Saturday evening at Kennedy Space Center in Florida, simulates launch day procedures by loading the 322-foot Space Launch System rocket with more than 700,000 gallons of super-cold liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen. If successful, the Artemis II mission could launch as early as February 8, sending four astronauts on a 10-day journey around the moon.[1][2][3]

items.title: Glencore nears Citi appointment for Rio Tinto merger talks

featured_image.name: Glencore close to appointing Citi as adviser for Rio Tinto ...

items.description:
Swiss miner Glencore is close to engaging Citigroup as its lead investment bank on its potential acquisition by Rio Tinto, a deal that could create the world's largest mining company worth over $200 billion, according to Reuters citing two people familiar with the matter.[1][2]

Citigroup Global Markets Inc. filed disclosures with the UK Takeover Panel in January, identifying itself as connected with Glencore in relation to a possible deal with Rio Tinto, according to filings made at the London Stock Exchange. Both Citi and Glencore declined to comment on the appointment.[3][2]

items.title: UK's Mandelson quits Labour as Epstein files trigger global fallout

featured_image.name: UK's Mandelson faces scrutiny over Epstein ties and leaked briefing

items.description:
The U.S. Department of Justice on Friday released over three million pages of documents, 180,000 images, and more than 2,000 videos from its investigation into convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, triggering resignations and political turmoil across multiple countries.

The massive disclosure, mandated by the Epstein Files Transparency Act signed by President Donald Trump in November 2025, represents the most extensive release since Congress passed the bipartisan legislation by overwhelming margins. Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche said Friday's release marked "the end of a very comprehensive document identification and review process."[1][2]

items.title: New transparent windows can shield buildings from EMP attacks

featured_image.name: Transparent windows can shield buildings from powerful ...

items.description:
Researchers from South Korea and the United States have developed transparent glass windows capable of shielding buildings from electromagnetic pulse threats, addressing a critical gap in defense technology for civilian and military infrastructure.

The breakthrough, led by Professor Chang Won Jung from the Department of Semiconductor Engineering at Seoul National University of Science and Technology (SeoulTech), employs an asymmetric hexagonal metal mesh film structure that delivers EMP protection while maintaining optical transparency. The research was published in Volume 72 of Engineering Science and Technology, an International Journal in December 2025.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Iran's president orders nuclear talks with US amid threats

featured_image.name: Masoud Pezeshkian: The reformist now Iran's president-elect

items.description: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian ordered the start of nuclear negotiations with the United States on Monday, with talks expected in Turkey in the coming days as both nations step back from the brink of military confrontation. The directive comes after weeks of escalating tensions following Iran's deadly crackdown on anti-government protests and President Donald Trump's deployment of an aircraft carrier strike group to the Middle East.

items.title: Iran summons EU ambassadors over terror designation of Guard

featured_image.name: EU labels Iran's Revolutionary Guard as 'terrorist organisation ...

items.description:
Iran summoned all European Union ambassadors in the country to formally protest the bloc's designation of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organization, escalating diplomatic tensions between Tehran and Brussels at a time of heightened regional instability.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei confirmed Monday that the summoning process began Sunday and continued into Monday, calling the EU's decision "illegal, unreasonable and very wrong." Baghaei said Iranian authorities are preparing reciprocal actions that will be sent to "decision-making bodies" in the coming days.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: OpenAI launches Codex desktop app for running parallel AI coding agents

featured_image.name: OpenAI brings its Codex coding app to Mac, with new multi-agent abilities included

items.description:
OpenAI on Monday unveiled a dedicated macOS desktop application for its Codex AI coding assistant, introducing what the company calls a "command center for agents" that enables software developers to run multiple AI coding assistants in parallel on long-running tasks.

The Codex app, available starting today, marks a departure from the command-line and browser-based interfaces that developers have used since Codex launched in April 2025. According to OpenAI, the desktop application is designed to address a fundamental shift in how developers work with AI—from pair programming with a single assistant to orchestrating teams of autonomous agents across projects.[1][2]

"This is the most loved internal product we've ever had," CEO Sam Altman said during a press briefing ahead of the launch. "It's been totally an amazing thing for us to be using recently at OpenAI".[1]

items.title: Anthropic partners with Allen Institute, HHMI on AI for science

featured_image.name: Anthropic CEO warns powerful AI with the brainpower of 50M ...

items.description:
Anthropic announced two new partnerships with the Allen Institute and Howard Hughes Medical Institute on Monday, signaling the AI company's deepening push into life sciences as it seeks to embed Claude-powered agents into scientific research workflows.

The collaborations, announced in an exclusive report by Fortune, will see the elite science labs use Anthropic's technology to address analysis, annotation, and coordination bottlenecks that can stretch research timelines into years. Rather than focusing on AI breakthroughs akin to Google DeepMind's AlphaFold, Anthropic is betting that its AI agents can accelerate the unglamorous but time-consuming work between discoveries.[1][2]

items.title: Trump cuts India tariffs to 18% after Modi pledges to halt Russian oil

featured_image.name: India gets friendship discount on Trump tariffs

items.description:
President Donald Trump announced Monday that the United States and India have reached an immediate trade deal following a phone call with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, lowering reciprocal tariffs from 25% to 18%. Under the agreement, India committed to stop buying Russian oil and purchase over $500 billion in US energy, technology, agricultural, and other products.[1][2]

The breakthrough marks a potential turning point in bilateral relations that had grown strained over the past year, with the US imposing steep 50% tariffs on Indian exports—among the highest applied to any country—in August 2025.[3][4]

items.title: US-Iran nuclear talks planned for Friday in Istanbul

featured_image.name: Steve Witkoff is involved in Middle East, Russia-Ukraine ...

items.description:
Turkey, Qatar, and Egypt are working to arrange urgent diplomatic talks between White House envoy Steve Witkoff and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, with a meeting planned for Friday in Istanbul, as escalating tensions between Washington and Tehran raise fears of a broader regional conflict.[1][2]

The diplomatic push comes as Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei warned Sunday that any U.S. attack would not remain limited. "The Americans should know that if they start a war, this time it will be a regional war," Khamenei said during a public address in Tehran. His comments followed the deployment of the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group to the Arabian Sea, which President Donald Trump has characterized as a "massive armada".[3][4][5][6][7]

items.title: QatarEnergy CEO says AI demand may flip LNG glut to shortage

featured_image.name: Qatar's North Field East gas expansion to begin output in mid-2026

items.description:
Rising electricity demand from artificial intelligence and data centers could flip the global liquefied natural gas market from projected oversupply to shortage by the end of the decade, QatarEnergy CEO Saad al-Kaabi warned at the opening of the LNG2026 conference in Doha on Monday.

"We always thought the market would have some kind of oversupply between 2025-2030 and beyond 2030 you will have a shortage," al-Kaabi said, adding that demand expectations have increased "mainly due to AI and data center requirements, which are sustained power requirements as a baseload."[1][2][3]

The warning comes as a record wave of LNG supply begins flowing from major projects in the United States and Qatar between 2026 and 2029, which had raised concerns among analysts about a supply glut that could depress prices. Projects like Golden Pass LNG on the U.S. Gulf Coast and Qatar's North Field Expansion are expected to contribute sizable new volumes.[4][5][6][1]

items.title: SpaceX in advanced talks to merge with xAI, sources say

featured_image.name: Elon Musk's xAI Raises $20 Billion - The New York Times

items.description: Elon Musk is moving rapidly to consolidate his business empire as SpaceX and artificial intelligence firm xAI have entered advanced discussions to merge, according to Bloomberg. The companies have already informed some of their investors about the plans, with an agreement potentially coming as soon as this week.[1]

items.title: Colombia's Petro arrives in Washington for Trump summit

featured_image.name: Colombia's President, an Outspoken Trump Critic, Heads to the White House

items.description: Colombian President Gustavo Petro arrived in Washington over the weekend ahead of his first face-to-face meeting with President Donald Trump, scheduled for Tuesday at the White House. The encounter aims to reset a bilateral relationship that has badly frayed over months of escalating tensions between two leaders known for their unpredictable natures.[1][2]

items.title: Pakistan says forces killed 145 militants in Balochistan

featured_image.name: Nearly 150 militants killed in 40-hour battle after deadly attacks in Pakistan

items.description:
Pakistan's security forces killed 145 militants over a 40-hour period following a wave of coordinated attacks across the southwestern province of Balochistan, marking one of the deadliest flare-ups in the region's decades-long separatist insurgency.

The violence, which erupted on Saturday across more than a dozen locations, left 17 law enforcement personnel and 31 civilians dead, according to Balochistan Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti, who addressed reporters in the provincial capital Quetta on Sunday.[1][2][3]

"We managed to kill 145 terrorists in 40 hours," Bugti said, describing the toll as the highest militant casualties in such a short span since Pakistan began its counterterrorism campaign. "The bodies of these 145 killed terrorists are in our custody, and some of them are Afghan nationals."[4][5][6]
